13.01.b:
- The oral examiner opens a film on a laptop with **no name on it** → you read it aloud, then he asks the next question
- **51 cases**, mixed order, every tumour and simulator of chapters 4–12; the favourites come two or three times in different bones
- Cover the answer → read the film in the six steps → say the sentence → check yourself in **Answers** (same case number)
- Each answer → model strip · spoken sentence · diagnosis with its source · differentials · the next question · the card to revise

**The six steps** (Handbook → 1 Reading the Film)

| Step | Choices (only these words) |
|---|---|
| 1 Site | epiphyseal · metaphyseal · diaphyseal (flat or short bone → its name) |
| 2 Centralization | central · eccentric · cortical · surface |
| 3 Behavior | osteolytic · osteosclerotic · mixed |
| 4 Margins | well-defined · ill-defined |
| 5 Cortical reaction | intact · thinning · expansion · destruction |
| 6 Special signs | the named sign or "none" |
| Verdict | benign latent · benign active · benign aggressive · malignant |

**The spoken sentence** (method section 4)

Say → "This is a(n) **[view]** X-ray of the **[bone]**, physis **[open / closed]**. There is a **[site]**, **[centralization]**, **[behavior]** lesion with **[margins]** margins. The cortex shows **[cortical reaction]**. **[Special sign]**. So this is a **[verdict]** lesion. In this age and site my differential is **A, B, C**. Next I would ask for **[next step]**."

Then → next step by the Handbook order: plain X-ray → MRI of the whole bone → bone scan → (malignant) metastatic work-up → **biopsy last** (→ 2 Work-up)

HIGH YIELD — three rules before every film
- **Age first** → <5 metastatic neuroblastoma, EG · 5–25 bone tumours and Ewing · >40 metastasis and myeloma first (→ 1 Incidence)
- **Epiphysis** → chondroblastoma before maturity, GCT after it (→ 1 Sites)
- **Pelvis** → immature Ewing · mature with calcification chondrosarcoma · mature without calcification metastasis (Nagah p31 → 1 Real Questions)

13.03.b:
#### Case 1

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| epiphyseal + metaphyseal | — | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | expansion | fibular head, subarticular | **benign aggressive** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the knee, physis closed. An **epiphyseal, osteolytic, expansile** lesion of the fibular head, well-defined without a sclerotic rim, no matrix. So → **benign aggressive**. In a 28-year-old my differential is **GCT**, ABC, chondroblastoma."
Then → "MRI of the whole bone, chest X-ray, then biopsy."
**Diagnosis** → giant cell tumour of the fibular head (Greenspan 7e, Fig 20.36)
**Differential** → ABC: younger, fluid–fluid levels · chondroblastoma: open physis, sclerotic rim, calcification · brown tumour: high calcium, several lesions
**Examiner asks** → "Treatment here?" → fibular head is expendable → en bloc resection, guard the common peroneal nerve, reattach the lateral collateral ligament and biceps
→ 5 GCT · 11

#### Case 2

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + interrupted periosteal reaction + soft-tissue mass | reaches the physis | **malignant** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the leg, physis open. A **metaphyseal–diaphyseal, central, mixed** lesion with **ill-defined** margins. The cortex is destroyed with an **interrupted periosteal reaction** and a soft-tissue mass. So → **malignant**. In an 11-year-old: **osteosarcoma**, Ewing sarcoma, osteomyelitis."
Then → "MRI of the whole tibia for skip lesions, chest CT, bone scan, then biopsy in the tumour centre."
**Diagnosis** → osteosarcoma of the tibia (Greenspan 7e, Fig 21.13)
**Differential** → Ewing: diaphyseal, onion skin, no tumour bone · osteomyelitis: fever, sequestrum, crosses the physis
**Examiner asks** → "Where do you biopsy?" → on the line of the definitive resection, through one compartment, by the surgeon who will resect
→ 9 Osteosarcoma · 8

#### Case 3

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning + healed fracture | abuts the physis | **benign active** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the humerus, physis open. A **metaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion with **well-defined** margins up to the physis. The cortex is **thin** with a healed fracture. So → **benign active**. In a 7-year-old: **simple bone cyst**, ABC, fibrous dysplasia."
Then → "No biopsy for a classic cyst; MRI only if in doubt."
**Diagnosis** → unicameral (simple) bone cyst of the proximal humerus (Orthopaedic Oncology, case 6, Fig 6-1)
**Differential** → ABC: eccentric, wider than the physis, fluid–fluid levels · fibrous dysplasia: ground glass, diaphyseal
**Examiner asks** → "Active or latent?" → within 1 cm of the physis = active (Campbell)
→ 4 Bone cysts · SBC 10

#### Case 4

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined (sclerotic rim) | intact | tract into the growth plate | **benign active** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the knee, physis open. A **metaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion of the proximal tibia, **well-defined** with a sclerotic rim. An osteolytic **tract runs into the growth plate**. So → **benign active**. In an 11-year-old: **Brodie abscess**, osteoid osteoma, chondroblastoma."
Then → "CRP, ESR, white count; MRI for the penumbra sign."
**Diagnosis** → subacute Brodie abscess of the proximal tibia (Greenspan 7e, Fig 25.10)
**Differential** → osteoid osteoma: cortical nidus, night pain · chondroblastoma: epiphyseal, calcification
**Examiner asks** → "Which sign proves infection on X-ray?" → the serpentine tract to the physis; on MRI the penumbra sign
→ 8 Simulators · Bone infection

#### Case 5

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | cortical | osteolytic | well-defined | intact | anterior tibial cortex, subtle | **malignant** |

Say → "Lateral X-ray of the tibia, physis closed. A subtle **diaphyseal, cortical, osteolytic** lesion of the **anterior cortex** with **well-defined** margins; cortex otherwise intact. With an anterior tibial cortex lesion I must think of a low-grade **malignant** tumour. Differential: **adamantinoma**, osteofibrous dysplasia, metastasis (past cancers)."
Then → "MRI of the whole tibia, bone scan, chest CT, then biopsy."
**Diagnosis** → adamantinoma of the mid-tibia (Orthopaedic Oncology, case 25, Fig 25-1)
**Differential** → osteofibrous dysplasia: child <10, bowing · metastasis: past breast cancer and melanoma, but anterior cortex of the tibia is the adamantinoma site
**Examiner asks** → "Treatment?" → wide resection only; curettage recurs
→ 12 Adamantinoma · 11

#### Case 6

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skull | — | osteolytic | well-defined (no rim) | destruction | multiple punched-out holes · mandible | **malignant** |

Say → "Lateral skull X-ray of an elderly woman: **multiple punched-out osteolytic** holes, well-defined **without sclerotic rims**, also in the mandible. So → **malignant**. Differential: **multiple myeloma**, metastases."
Then → "Serum and urine electrophoresis, calcium, creatinine; skeletal survey — the bone scan may be cold."
**Diagnosis** → multiple myeloma of the skull (Greenspan 7e, Fig 22.38)
**Differential** → metastasis: holes of different sizes · hyperparathyroidism: salt and pepper, no discrete holes
**Examiner asks** → "Why skeletal survey not bone scan?" → myeloma is often cold on bone scan
→ 11 Myeloma · 6 · 1 Real Questions

#### Case 7

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | thinning | long diaphyseal focus | **benign latent** |

Say → "AP X-rays of the humerus, physis open. A **diaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion, **well-defined**, cortex **thinned**, no periosteal reaction. So → **benign latent**. In a 13-year-old: **fibrous dysplasia**, simple bone cyst, NOF."
Then → "No biopsy if classic; bone scan to look for other lesions."
**Diagnosis** → monostotic fibrous dysplasia of the humerus (Greenspan 7e, Fig 19.22)
**Differential** → SBC: metaphyseal, fallen fragment · NOF: eccentric, scalloped rim
**Examiner asks** → "Café-au-lait spots and early puberty?" → McCune-Albright syndrome
→ 8 Fibrous dysplasia · 6

#### Case 8

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | expansion + thinning | femoral neck | **benign active** |

Say → "AP pelvis of a child: a **metaphyseal, osteolytic, expansile** lesion of the femoral neck, **well-defined**, cortex thin. So → **benign active**. Differential: **ABC**, simple bone cyst, fibrous dysplasia."
Then → "MRI for fluid–fluid levels, then biopsy — always for ABC."
**Diagnosis** → aneurysmal bone cyst of the femoral neck (Orthopaedic Oncology, case 14, Fig 14-1)
**Differential** → SBC: central, not wider than the physis, fallen fragment · telangiectatic osteosarcoma: no rim, soft-tissue mass
**Examiner asks** → "Why biopsy?" → to exclude telangiectatic osteosarcoma and a host lesion (secondary ABC)
→ 4 Bone cysts · ABC 8

#### Case 9

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | surface | mixed | well-defined | cortex continuous with the host | erodes the fibula | **benign active** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the distal leg, physis closed. A **metaphyseal surface** bony projection from the posterolateral tibia, **well-defined**, its cortex and medulla **continuous with the host**; it **erodes the fibula**. So → **benign active**. Differential: **osteochondroma**, parosteal osteosarcoma."
Then → "CT or MRI for the cartilage cap and the fibula."
**Diagnosis** → osteochondroma of the distal tibia eroding the fibula (Greenspan 7e, Fig 16.70)
**Differential** → parosteal osteosarcoma: dense mass, no medullary continuity · periosteal chondroma: saucer erosion
**Examiner asks** → "Indications to excise?" → pain, pressure on a bone, nerve or vessel, deformity, growth after maturity, a thick cap in an adult
→ 6 Osteochondroma · 11

#### Case 10

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vertebral body | — | osteosclerotic | well-defined | intact | ivory vertebra · paraspinal bulge | **malignant** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the lower thoracic spine of a 32-year-old: one **dense ivory vertebra** (T7) with a **bulging paraspinal line**, disc spaces kept. So → **malignant** until proved otherwise. Differential: **lymphoma**, blastic metastasis, Paget disease."
Then → "MRI, CT chest–abdomen, bone marrow biopsy, then vertebral biopsy."
**Diagnosis** → lymphoma, sclerotic T7 (Greenspan 7e, Fig 22.22)
**Differential** → Paget: vertebra enlarged, picture frame · blastic metastasis: older, prostate or breast
**Examiner asks** → "Treatment of primary bone lymphoma?" → chemotherapy ± radiotherapy; surgery only for fracture or cord compression
→ 12 Lymphoma · 6

#### Case 11

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pedicle | — | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction | missing pedicle (winking owl) | **benign aggressive or malignant** |

Say → "AP X-ray of the thoracic spine of a 12-year-old: **one pedicle has disappeared** — the winking owl sign. That is pedicle destruction by a lesion. In a child: **osteoblastoma**, ABC, EG; in an adult metastasis first."
Then → "MRI for cord and extent, CT for matrix, then biopsy."
**Diagnosis** → osteoblastoma of the T10 pedicle (Orthopaedic Oncology, case 33, Fig 33-3: "beware the missing pedicle")
**Differential** → ABC: blow-out, fluid–fluid levels · metastasis: adult, pedicle lost early (lung carcinoma example in chapter 11)
**Examiner asks** → "What is the winking owl?" → loss of one pedicle on the AP film = pedicle lysis, highly suggestive of tumour (OKU Tumors 4)
→ 11 Bone metastasis · winking owl · 7 Osteoblastoma

#### Case 12

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| metaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | chondroid calcification in the mass | **malignant** |

Say → "AP and lateral X-rays of the elbow of a 55-year-old: a lesion of the proximal ulna with a **huge soft-tissue mass full of chondroid (rings and arcs) calcification**, ill-defined. So → **malignant**. Differential: **chondrosarcoma**, osteosarcoma, metastasis."
Then → "MRI, chest CT, biopsy along the resection line."
**Diagnosis** → chondrosarcoma of the proximal ulna (Greenspan 7e, Fig 21.50)
**Differential** → osteosarcoma: younger, cloud-like tumour bone · metastasis: no chondroid matrix
**Examiner asks** → "Chemotherapy or radiotherapy?" → conventional chondrosarcoma is resistant to both → wide resection
→ 10 Chondrosarcoma · 11 · real question 23

#### Case 13

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | well-defined | pathological fracture | single lesion on bone scan | **benign aggressive** |
